t: 3684 — Maximize Sum of At Most K Distinct Elements
o: Pick at most k distinct values from nums maximizing their sum, returned in strictly descending order. Clearly the optimum takes the k largest distinct values: deduplicate, sort descending, slice k.
k: Greedy: the k largest distinct values maximize the sum.
Output must be strictly descending, which a descending sort of distinct values provides.

a.n: Approach 1: Deduplicate, sort descending, take k
a.i: After deduplication every candidate is usable at most once, and taking the largest k is trivially optimal for maximizing the sum. Sorting the distinct values descending and slicing the first k yields the required output format directly.
s: Convert nums to a set and sort its elements descending.
Take the first min(k, size) elements.
a.t: O(n log n) — dedup is linear, sorting the distinct values dominates

w: A partial-selection alternative (quickselect or a size-k min-heap) gives O(n log k) if n were huge, but at n ≤ 100 the sort is simplest. Edge cases: k larger than the number of distinct values (return all of them, Example 3), and ensuring strict descent (guaranteed by dedup).
